III. Part XXII deals with the Short Title, Commencement, Authoritative Text in Hindi and Repeals, and was original.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Parts XX, XXI and XXII were original; Part XXII covers the Short Title, Commencement, Authoritative Text in Hindi and Repeals.

7.title: Prime Minister: Powers and Constitutional Position

mcqs.question: Article 74 of the Constitution provides for:
options: The 15% limit on the size of the Council of Ministers
The duties of the Prime Minister
The Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
The appointment and tenure of Ministers
mcqs.explanation: Article 74 provides for the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Prime Minister is the real Executive Head of the Union.
The Prime Minister can be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister is responsible to the Rajya Sabha.
The Prime Minister is appointed by the President.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that the Prime Minister is responsible to the Rajya Sabha. The Prime Minister is responsible only to the Lok Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Prime Minister is the real Executive Head of the Union.
Reason (R): The President is the nominal or constitutional head.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President is the nominal or constitutional head, while the Prime Minister functions as the real Executive Head of the Union.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The oath of the Prime Minister is administered by the President.
Statement B: The resignation of the Prime Minister is addressed to the President.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true: the President administers the Prime Minister’s oath, and the Prime Minister addresses resignation to the President.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following bodies are chaired by the Prime Minister?
I. NITI Aayog
II. National Development Council
III. National Integration Council
IV. Inter-State Council
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Minister is the Chairman of NITI Aayog, the National Development Council, the National Integration Council and the Inter-State Council.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Article 74
 b. Article 75
 c. Article 78
 d. Article 75(3)

List-II
 i. Appointment, tenure and responsibility of Ministers
 ii. Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President
 iii. Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha
 iv. Duties of the Prime Minister
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-i, c-iv and d-iii. Article 74 concerns aid and advice, Article 75 concerns Ministers, Article 78 concerns the Prime Minister’s duties, and Article 75(3) concerns collective responsibility.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements regarding the size of the Council of Ministers are correct?
1. The total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
2. The same 15% limit applies to the States, including the Chief Minister.
3. The 15% limit was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
4. Article 75(1A) contains the 15% limit.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The 15% limit, applicable to the Union and the States, was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, and is referred to in Article 75(1A).

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): If a No-Confidence Motion is passed, the entire Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, must resign.
Reason (R): The Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha means that the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, must resign when a No-Confidence Motion is passed.

mcqs.question: Who is the head of the Council of Ministers?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha.
Statement B: The Prime Minister is normally the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha and is normally the leader of the majority party there.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): A person need not be a member of Parliament at the time of appointment as Prime Minister.
Reason (R): The person appointed as Prime Minister must become a member of Parliament within six months under Article 75(5).
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: A person may be appointed without being an MP, but must become a member of Parliament within six months under Article 75(5). This requirement explains the stated position.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are powers of the Prime Minister as head of the Council of Ministers?
1. Selecting Ministers
2. Allocating portfolios to Ministers
3. Asking any Minister to resign
mcqs.explanation: All three listed functions belong to the Prime Minister as head of the Council of Ministers: selecting Ministers, allocating portfolios and asking a Minister to resign.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Communicating all decisions of the Council of Ministers
 b. Furnishing information required by the President
 c. Submitting a matter for reconsideration of the Council of Ministers
 d. Acting as the link between the President and the Council of Ministers

List-II
 i. When the President so requires
 ii. A general coordinating link
 iii. Information sought by the President
 iv. Decisions of the Council of Ministers
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: communicating decisions—a-iv; furnishing required information—b-iii; submitting matters for reconsideration when required—c-i; and acting as the link—d-ii.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Prime Minister is the leader of the Lok Sabha.
II. The Prime Minister is the Leader of the House.
III. The Prime Minister is the chief spokesperson of the Government.
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Minister is described as the leader of the Lok Sabha, the Leader of the House and the chief spokesperson of the Government.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. NITI Aayog
 b. Planning Commission
 c. National Disaster Management Authority
 d. National Development Council

List-II
 i. Earlier body chaired by the Prime Minister
 ii. Body chaired by the Prime Minister
 iii. Body chaired by the Prime Minister
 iv. Body chaired by the Prime Minister
mcqs.explanation: The Planning Commission was the earlier body chaired by the Prime Minister before NITI Aayog. NITI Aayog, the National Disaster Management Authority and the National Development Council are chaired by the Prime Minister.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Prime Minister advises the President on the appointment of other Ministers.
II. The Prime Minister advises the President on the summoning and prorogation of Parliament.
III. The Prime Minister advises the President on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
IV. The Prime Minister advises the President on the declaration of Emergency through the recommendation of the Cabinet.
V. The Prime Minister advises the President on the appointment of the Chief Justice of India.
options: II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III and IV only
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II, III and IV are correct. The listed functions do not include advising the President on the appointment of the Chief Justice of India.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India.
Statement B: Jawaharlal Nehru was the longest-serving Prime Minister of India.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru is identified as both the first Prime Minister of India and the longest-serving Prime Minister of India.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I

a. Indira Gandhi
b. Morarji Desai
c. Indira Gandhi initially as Prime Minister
d. Manmohan Singh

List-II

i. First woman Prime Minister of India
ii. First non-Congress Prime Minister of India
iii. Initially a member of the Rajya Sabha as Prime Minister
iv. Member of the Rajya Sabha as Prime Minister

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mcqs.explanation: Indira Gandhi was the first woman Prime Minister of India and was initially a Rajya Sabha member as Prime Minister. Morarji Desai was the first non-Congress Prime Minister, while Manmohan Singh was a Rajya Sabha member as Prime Minister.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Deputy Prime Minister is not a constitutional post.
Statement B: The Deputy Prime Minister is only a political post.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The Deputy Prime Minister is not a constitutional post; it is only a political post.

mcqs.question: Article 52 of the Constitution provides for:
options: The executive power of the Union
The term of office of the President
mcqs.explanation: Article 52 provides that there shall be a President of India. Article 53 deals with the executive power of the Union.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the election of the President is incorrect?
options: Disputes regarding the presidential election are decided finally by the Supreme Court.
Nominated members of Parliament participate in the election of the President.
The President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College.
Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry are part of the Electoral College.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that nominated members of Parliament participate. Nominated members of Parliament and State Legislative Councils do not participate in the presidential election.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President is the nominal or constitutional head of the State.
Reason (R): The real executive is the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President is the constitutional head, while the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister constitutes the real executive.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 52
(b) Article 53
(c) Article 72
(d) Article 123

List-II
(i) Executive power of the Union vested in the President
(ii) There shall be a President of India
(iii) Power to grant pardons and related relief
(iv) Ordinance-making power
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-i, c-iii and d-iv. These correspond respectively to Articles 52, 53, 72 and 123.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the presidential election:
I. It is an indirect election.
II. It uses proportional representation by means of the Single Transferable Vote and secret ballot.
III. Nominated members of Parliament participate in it.
IV. Disputes regarding the election are decided by the Supreme Court.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and IV are correct. Nominated members of Parliament do not participate in the presidential election, making Statement III incorrect.

mcqs.question: The resignation of the President is addressed to the:
mcqs.explanation: The President addresses the resignation to the Vice-President.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding vacancy in the office of the President is incorrect?
options: In case of death, resignation, removal or otherwise, the Vice-President acts as President.
If both the offices of President and Vice-President are vacant, the Chief Justice of India or the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court acts as President.
If both offices are vacant, the Prime Minister acts as President.
The Vice-President acts as President under Article 65 in the specified circumstances.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that the Prime Minister acts as President. If both offices are vacant, the Chief Justice of India or the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court acts as President.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies participate in the election of the President.
Reason (R): Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in the impeachment of the President.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the non-participation of elected State Assembly members in impeachment does not explain their participation in the presidential election.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The President can seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court, but that opinion is not binding.
Statement B: The President can return a Bill only once, except a Money Bill.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. The President may seek a non-binding advisory opinion under Article 143 and may return a Bill only once, except a Money Bill.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(b) Pratibha Patil
(c) Droupadi Murmu
(d) Chief Justice of India

List-II
(i) First Woman President
(ii) First President
(iii) Oath administrator to the President
(iv) First Tribal President
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Dr. Rajendra Prasad—First President, Pratibha Patil—First Woman President, Droupadi Murmu—First Tribal President, and Chief Justice of India—oath administrator.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following Articles relate to the emergency powers of the President?
1. Article 352
2. Article 356
3. Article 360
4. Article 143
mcqs.explanation: Three Articles—352, 356 and 360—relate to National Emergency, President’s Rule and Financial Emergency respectively. Article 143 concerns the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court.

mcqs.question: The President promulgates Ordinances when:
options: The Supreme Court is not in session
The Council of Ministers is not in office
The Lok Sabha has been dissolved permanently
mcqs.explanation: The President promulgates Ordinances when Parliament is not in session. The ordinance-making power is co-extensive with the legislative power of Parliament.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements correctly describe the President of India?
1. The executive power of the Union is exercised by the President directly or through officers subordinate to the President.
2. The President is the First Citizen of India.
3. The President is a symbol of the unity of the nation.
4. The President is a symbol of the integrity of the nation.
5. The President is a symbol of the solidarity of the nation.
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. The President exercises the Union’s executive power directly or through subordinate officers and is described as the First Citizen and a symbol of the nation’s unity, integrity and solidarity.

mcqs.question: Under Article 53(2), the President of India is the:
options: Final authority in disputes regarding presidential election
Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces
Chief executive of the Council of Ministers
mcqs.explanation: Article 53(2) identifies the President as the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Elected members of the Lok Sabha
(b) Elected members of the Rajya Sabha
(c) Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States
(d) Legislative Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry

List-II
(i) Included in the Presidential Electoral College
(ii) Included in the Presidential Electoral College
(iii) Included in the Presidential Electoral College
(iv) Added to the Presidential Electoral College by the 70th Amendment
mcqs.explanation: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies form part of the Electoral College. Delhi and Puducherry were included by the 70th Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The value of an MLA’s vote is calculated to ensure uniformity among the States.
Reason (R): The value of an MP’s vote is calculated to ensure parity between the Union and the States.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but they describe two distinct principles: uniformity among the States for MLA votes and parity between the Union and the States for MP votes.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Citizenship requirement
(b) Minimum age requirement
(c) Legislative qualification
(d) Office-related restriction

List-II
(i) Must be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
(ii) Must not hold any office of profit
(iii) Must be a citizen of India
(iv) Must have completed 35 years of age
mcqs.explanation: A presidential candidate must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, qualified for election to the Lok Sabha and must not hold an office of profit.

mcqs.question: Under Article 57, the President of India is:
options: Eligible for re-election any number of times
Eligible for re-election for two terms only
mcqs.explanation: Article 57 permits the President to be re-elected any number of times.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the impeachment of the President:
I. The President can be removed by impeachment for violation of the Constitution.
II. Article 61 deals with the impeachment of the President.
III. Either House of Parliament can prefer a charge for impeachment.
IV. A special majority is required in both Houses of Parliament.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. Impeachment for violation of the Constitution is dealt with under Article 61; either House may prefer the charge, and a special majority is required in both Houses.

mcqs.question: Which enactment deals with succession when both the offices of President and Vice-President are vacant?
options: The Representation of the People Act
mcqs.explanation: The President’s Succession Act deals with succession when both the offices of President and Vice-President are vacant.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Prime Minister
(b) Other Ministers
(c) Governors
(d) Judges of the Supreme Court

List-II
(i) Appointed by the President
(ii) Appointed by the President
(iii) Appointed by the President
(iv) Appointed by the President
mcqs.explanation: The President appoints the Prime Minister, other Ministers, Governors and Judges of the Supreme Court.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Judges of the High Courts
(b) Comptroller and Auditor General
(c) Attorney General
(d) Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
(e) Members of the Union Public Service Commission
(f) Election Commissioners
(g) Members of the Finance Commission

List-II
(i) Attorney General
(ii) Comptroller and Auditor General
(iii) Judges of the High Courts
(iv) Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission
(v) Members of the Union Public Service Commission
(vi) Election Commissioners
(vii) Members of the Finance Commission
options: a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i, e-v, f-vii, g-vi
a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv, e-vii, f-vi, g-v
a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-v, e-iv, f-vii, g-vi
a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv, e-v, f-vi, g-vii
mcqs.explanation: The President appoints Judges of the High Courts, the CAG, the Attorney General, the UPSC Chairman and members, Election Commissioners, and members of the Finance Commission. Therefore, option 1 gives all the correct pairs.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President normally appoints the leader of the majority party as Prime Minister.
Reason (R): The President can seek information from the Prime Minister under Article 78.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President normally appoints the leader of the majority party as Prime Minister, while Article 78 enables the President to seek information from the Prime Minister; the latter does not explain the former.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The President is an integral part of Parliament under Article 79.
II. The President summons and prorogues Parliament and dissolves the Lok Sabha.
III. The President addresses Parliament under Article 87.
IV. The President assents to Bills under Article 111.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The President is an integral part of Parliament, summons and prorogues it, dissolves the Lok Sabha, addresses Parliament under Article 87, and assents to Bills under Article 111.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the veto powers of the President:

I. The President has the power of absolute veto.
II. The President has the power of suspensive veto.
III. The President has the power of pocket veto.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: The President has all three veto powers listed: absolute veto, suspensive veto and pocket veto.

mcqs.question: How many members does the President nominate to the Rajya Sabha?
mcqs.explanation: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The President appoints Judges of the Supreme Court.
Statement B: The President appoints Judges of the High Courts.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The President appoints Judges of the Supreme Court as well as Judges of the High Courts.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are powers of the President under Article 72?

1. Granting reprieves
2. Granting respites
3. Granting remissions
4. Suspending sentences
mcqs.explanation: All four listed powers are included under Article 72: the President can grant reprieves, respites and remissions, and can suspend sentences.

mcqs.question: The term of office of the President of India is prescribed as five years under which Article of the Constitution?
mcqs.explanation: The President holds office for five years under Article 56.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the military and diplomatic powers of the President:
I. The President declares war on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
II. The President concludes peace on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
III. The President appoints Ambassadors.
IV. The President appoints High Commissioners.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: The President declares war and concludes peace on the advice of the Council of Ministers, and appoints Ambassadors and High Commissioners.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are listed as limited discretionary powers of the President?
1. Appointing a Prime Minister in case of a hung Parliament
2. Dismissing a government that has lost its majority
3. Dissolving the Lok Sabha
4. Appointing Ambassadors
mcqs.explanation: The first three are listed as important limited discretionary powers. Appointment of Ambassadors is a diplomatic power, not one of the listed limited discretionary powers.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President may return the advice of the Council of Ministers for reconsideration once.
Reason (R): This power was provided by the 44th Amendment.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The President may return the advice of the Council of Ministers once for reconsideration, and this power was provided by the 44th Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(b) Pratibha Patil
(c) Droupadi Murmu
(d) Emoluments of the President

List-II
(i) Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
(ii) First Tribal President and 15th President
(iii) Longest-serving President; served two terms
(iv) First Woman President; 12th / 14th by the stated tenure count
mcqs.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the longest-serving President and served two terms; Pratibha Patil was the first woman President and is stated as the 12th / 14th by tenure count; Droupadi Murmu was the first Tribal President and the 15th President. Presidential emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The President holds Rank 1 in the Order of Precedence.
Statement B: The President is the Head of the State, not the Head of the Government.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The President holds Rank 1 in the Order of Precedence. The President is the Head of the State, while the President is not the Head of the Government.

mcqs.question: Article 63 of the Constitution provides for which of the following?
options: The office of the President of India
The office of the Vice-President of India
The term of office of the Vice-President
mcqs.explanation: Article 63 provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India.

mcqs.question: Who constitutes the Electoral College for the election of the Vice-President of India?
options: Members of Parliament and members of State Legislative Assemblies
Elected members of both Houses of Parliament only
Members of both Houses of Parliament, elected as well as nominated
Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies and Parliament
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-President is elected by members of both Houses of Parliament, including elected and nominated members. State Legislative Assemblies do not participate.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the removal of the Vice-President is incorrect?
options: The resolution must be agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
The removal resolution is passed by the Rajya Sabha.
The resolution is passed by a simple majority of the Rajya Sabha.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the type of majority. The Rajya Sabha resolution requires a majority of all the then members of the Council, not a simple majority.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Reason (R): Article 64 provides for the Vice-President to hold this position.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 64 specifically provides that the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Article 63
(b) Article 64
(c) Article 66
(d) Article 67

List-II
(i) Office of the Vice-President
(ii) Term of office
(iii) Ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
(iv) Election of the Vice-President
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Article 63—office of the Vice-President; Article 64—ex-officio Chairman; Article 66—election; Article 67—term of office.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the election of the Vice-President:

I. Members of both Houses of Parliament, elected as well as nominated, participate.
II. State Legislative Assemblies participate.
III. The election uses proportional representation by means of the Single Transferable Vote.
IV. The election is conducted by secret ballot.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, III and IV are correct. State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in the Vice-Presidential election.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Vice-President addresses his resignation to the President.
Statement B: The oath of the Vice-President is administered by the President.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Vice-President resigns by addressing the President, and the oath is administered by the President.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are qualifications prescribed for election as Vice-President?

1. Citizen of India
2. Completed 35 years of age
3. Qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
4. Does not hold any office of profit
mcqs.explanation: Three listed conditions are correct: Indian citizenship, completion of 35 years, and not holding an office of profit. The Vice-President must be qualified for election as a Rajya Sabha member, not a Lok Sabha member.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum period for which the Vice-President may act as President when the office of President falls vacant or the President is unable to discharge functions?
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-President may act as President for a maximum period of six months, within which the election for a new President must be held.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Constitutional position of the Vice-President in the Order of Precedence
(b) Model for the office of the Vice-President
(c) First Vice-President of India
(d) Re-election of the Vice-President

List-II
(i) Dr. S. Radhakrishnan
(ii) American Vice-President
(iii) Any number of times
(iv) Second-highest constitutional office after the President
mcqs.explanation: The Vice-President is the second-highest constitutional office after the President, and the office is modelled on the American Vice-President. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President, and the Vice-President is eligible for re-election any number of times.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court decides all doubts and disputes regarding the election of the Vice-President.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court’s decision regarding the Vice-Presidential election is final.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Article 71 provides that the Supreme Court decides all doubts and disputes regarding the Vice-Presidential election. Its decision is final, but that finality does not explain the Court’s authority to decide the disputes.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Vice-President is eligible for re-election any number of times.
II. The Vice-President presides over the sittings of the Rajya Sabha.
III. The Vice-President has a casting vote in case of a tie in the Rajya Sabha.
IV. The Vice-President does not preside when a resolution for his removal is under consideration.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The Vice-President may be re-elected any number of times and, as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, presides over its sittings, exercises a casting vote in a tie, and does not preside during consideration of a resolution for his removal.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are circumstances mentioned in which the President’s office may fall vacant or the President may be unable to discharge functions?

1. Death
2. Resignation
3. Removal
4. Absence
5. Illness
mcqs.explanation: All five listed circumstances are covered: death, resignation and removal may cause the office of the President to fall vacant, while absence and illness may prevent the President from discharging functions.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Vice-President draws salary and allowances as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and these are not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India as Vice-President.
Statement B: When acting as President, the Vice-President is entitled to the President’s salary, allowances and privileges.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: As Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Vice-President draws salary and allowances, which are not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India in the capacity of Vice-President. When acting as President, the Vice-President receives the President’s salary, allowances and privileges.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Presidential Electoral College consists of Members of Parliament and Members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories.
II. The qualification for election as President is linked to eligibility for the Lok Sabha.
III. The President is removed by impeachment by both Houses of Parliament.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Presidential Electoral College includes Members of Parliament and Members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories; the President’s qualification is linked to Lok Sabha eligibility; and removal is by impeachment by both Houses of Parliament.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The President is an integral part of Parliament.
Statement B: The Vice-President is not a part of Parliament.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: The President is an integral part of Parliament, whereas the Vice-President is not a part of Parliament.

mcqs.question: To whom does the President address the resignation?
options: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
mcqs.explanation: The President addresses the resignation to the Vice-President.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Dr. S. Radhakrishnan — longest-serving Vice-President
(b) Dr. S. Radhakrishnan — number of terms served as Vice-President
(c) Mohammad Hamid Ansari — distinction relating to terms as Vice-President
(d) Dr. S. Radhakrishnan — position in the sequence of Vice-Presidents

List-II
(i) Two full terms
(ii) First Vice-President
(iii) Longest-serving Vice-President
(iv) Two terms
mcqs.explanation: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the longest-serving Vice-President and served two terms. Mohammad Hamid Ansari was the only person to serve two full terms, while Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Vice-President is incorrect?
options: Nominated Members of Parliament do not vote in the election of the Vice-President.
The Vice-President is elected and is not appointed by the President.
State Legislative Assembly members do not vote in the election of the Vice-President.
The Vice-President does not take part in the election of the President as a nominated member.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that nominated Members of Parliament do not vote in the Vice-Presidential election. Nominated MPs do vote in the Vice-Presidential election, while the Vice-President does not take part in the Presidential election as a nominated member.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Vice-President is not a member of either House of Parliament.
Statement B: The salary of the Vice-President in the capacity of Vice-President is not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Vice-President is not a member of either House of Parliament, and the salary drawn in the capacity of Vice-President is not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

10.title: Chief Minister: Powers, Articles and Key Facts

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional position of the Chief Minister in a State?
options: The Chief Minister is the real executive head, while the Governor is the nominal or constitutional head
The Chief Minister is the nominal head, while the Governor is the real executive head
The Chief Minister and Governor are jointly the real executive heads
The Governor is the head of the Council of Ministers, while the Chief Minister is its nominal head
mcqs.explanation: The Chief Minister is the real executive head of the State and heads the State Council of Ministers. The Governor is the nominal or constitutional head.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Chief Minister acts as a link between the Governor and the State Council of Ministers.
Reason (R): Article 167 requires the Chief Minister to communicate decisions of the Council of Ministers and proposals for legislation to the Governor.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The communication and information-related duties specified under Article 167 explain the Chief Minister’s linking role between the Governor and the Council of Ministers.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Governor is the head of the State, while the Chief Minister is the head of the Government
In the case of a hung Assembly, the Governor has discretionary power in appointing the Chief Minister
The Chief Minister advises the Governor on the appointment of other Ministers
The Chief Minister is responsible only to the Legislative Council
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is 'Legislative Council'. The Chief Minister is responsible only to the Legislative Assembly, not to the Legislative Council.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and is normally the leader of the majority party in the Legislative Assembly.
Statement B: A person appointed Chief Minister need not be a member of the State Legislature at the time of appointment, but must become a member within six months.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, normally choosing the majority party leader, and a non-member must enter the State Legislature within six months.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the size of the State Council of Ministers:
I. The total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
II. The minimum strength in smaller States is 12, including the Chief Minister.
III. The 15% limit is calculated on the total strength of the Legislative Council.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct under the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003. Statement III is incorrect because the limit is based on the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) First woman Chief Minister
(b) First non-Congress Chief Minister
(c) Chief Minister of Delhi/Puducherry
(d) Oath of the Chief Minister administered by

List-II
(i) President
(ii) Sucheta Kripalani
(iii) Governor
(iv) E.M.S. Namboodiripad
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: (a)-ii, Sucheta Kripalani; (b)-iv, E.M.S. Namboodiripad; (c)-i, President; and (d)-iii, Governor.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are associated with the Governor?
1. The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor.
2. The oath of the Chief Minister is administered by the Governor.
3. The resignation of the Chief Minister is addressed to the Governor.
4. The Chief Minister of Delhi/Puducherry is appointed by the Governor.
mcqs.explanation: The first three statements are correct. The Chief Minister of Delhi/Puducherry is appointed by the President under Article 239AA, so statement 4 is incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
Reason (R): If a No-Confidence Motion is passed, the entire Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, must resign.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The requirement that the entire Council, including the Chief Minister, resign after losing a No-Confidence Motion reflects its collective responsibility to the Legislative Assembly under Article 164(2).

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Article 163 provides for a Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor.
Statement B: Article 163 concerns the Council of Ministers aiding and advising the Governor.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements correctly describe Article 163, which provides for the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister to aid and advise the Governor.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Selects Ministers
(b) Allocates portfolios
(c) Recommends removal of a Minister
(d) Furnishes information required by the Governor

List-II
(i) Power relating to the composition of the Council of Ministers
(ii) Power relating to distribution of ministerial responsibilities
(iii) Power to seek removal of a Minister
(iv) Duty towards the Governor
mcqs.explanation: The Chief Minister selects Ministers, allocates portfolios, can recommend removal of any Minister, and furnishes information required by the Governor. Thus, the correct pairs are a-i, b-ii, c-iii and d-iv.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the membership position of the Chief Minister in a State?
options: The Chief Minister must always be a member of the Legislative Assembly
The Chief Minister may be a member of the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council if the State has one
The Chief Minister cannot be a member of the State Legislature
The Chief Minister must always be a member of the Legislative Council
mcqs.explanation: The Chief Minister may be a member of the Legislative Assembly or, where the State has one, the Legislative Council.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Chief Minister submits for the consideration of the Council of Ministers any matter decided by a Minister that has not been considered by the Council.
Reason (R): The Chief Minister furnishes information required by the Governor.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true duties of the Chief Minister. However, furnishing information to the Governor does not explain the separate duty of placing before the Council a matter decided by a Minister but not considered by the Council.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Leader of the Legislative Assembly
(b) Chief spokesperson of the State Government
(c) Advice on summoning and prorogation of the State Legislature
(d) Advice on dissolution of the Legislative Assembly

List-II
(i) Leadership role in the Legislative Assembly
(ii) Public communication role of the State Government
(iii) Advice concerning the sittings of the State Legislature
(iv) Advice concerning ending the term of the Legislative Assembly
mcqs.explanation: The Chief Minister is the leader of the Legislative Assembly and the chief spokesperson of the State Government. The Chief Minister also advises the Governor on summoning and prorogation of the State Legislature and on dissolution of the Legislative Assembly.

mcqs.question: Under which Article is the Governor appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal?
mcqs.explanation: Article 155 provides that the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the qualifications of the Governor is incorrect?
options: The person must have completed 35 years of age.
The person must be a citizen of India.
The person should not hold any office of profit.
The person may continue as a member of Parliament after becoming Governor.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is that a Governor may continue as a member of Parliament. A Governor should not be a member of Parliament or a State Legislature; if already a member, the person must vacate the seat.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The normal term of office of a Governor is five years, but the Governor may leave office earlier or continue longer.
Reason (R): The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Although the normal term is five years, the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President, permitting earlier removal or continuation beyond five years.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Governor is the nominal or constitutional head of the State.
Statement B: The real executive authority is exercised by the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the constitutional position of the Governor described in the notes.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The emoluments and allowances of the Governor are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
II. If the same person is Governor of two or more States, the salary is shared in the proportion determined by the President.
III. The oath of the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The notes connect the Governor’s salary with the State Consolidated Fund, provide for Presidential determination of shared salary, and assign oath administration to the concerned High Court’s Chief Justice.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 153
(b) Article 154
(c) Article 159
(d) Article 213

List-II
(i) Oath of the Governor
(ii) Governor for each State
(iii) Executive power of the State vested in the Governor
(iv) Promulgation of Ordinances
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iii, c-i and d-iv.

mcqs.question: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor?
options: The Chief Justice of the concerned High Court
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
The Chief Minister of the State
mcqs.explanation: Under Article 159, the oath of the Governor is administered by the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Governor’s pardoning power is limited to offences against State laws.
Reason (R): Article 161 provides the Governor with the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions, and to suspend or commute sentences.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason only describes the types of relief available under Article 161; it does not explain the specific limitation to offences against State laws.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.
Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal.
Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of an independent State.
mcqs.explanation: The altered detail is the State. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh, whereas Padmaja Naidu was the first woman Governor of West Bengal and the first woman Governor of an independent State.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are discretionary powers of the Governor?
1. Appointment of the Chief Minister in case of a hung Assembly
2. Dismissal of a Council of Ministers that has lost its majority
3. Reserving a Bill for the consideration of the President
4. Recommending President’s Rule under Article 356
mcqs.explanation: All four listed actions are included among the Governor’s discretionary powers.

mcqs.question:
Match the features in List-I with the corresponding provisions or descriptions in List-II:
List-I
(a) Appointment of the Governor
(b) Removal of the Governor
(c) Ordinance-making power of the Governor
(d) Pardoning power of the Governor

List-II
(i) Pleasure of the President
(ii) Article 213
(iii) Electoral College
(iv) Article 161
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-i, c-ii and d-iv: the Governor is appointed by the President, holds office during the President’s pleasure, promulgates Ordinances under Article 213, and exercises pardoning power under Article 161.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Other Ministers
(b) Advocate-General
(c) State Election Commissioner
(d) Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commission

List-II
(i) Appointed by the Governor
(ii) Appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister
(iii) Appointed by the Governor
(iv) Appointed by the Governor
mcqs.explanation: The Governor appoints other Ministers on the advice of the Chief Minister. The Advocate-General, State Election Commissioner, and Chairman and members of the State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The Governor can seek information from the Chief Minister under Article 167.
II. The Governor is an integral part of the State Legislature under Article 168.
III. The Governor summons the State Legislature.
IV. The Governor prorogues the State Legislature.
V. The Governor dissolves the Legislative Assembly.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: I, II, III, IV and V
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. These are among the Governor’s executive and legislative powers, including the power to seek information under Article 167 and to summon, prorogue, and dissolve the State Legislature or Legislative Assembly.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Governor addresses the State Legislature under Article 176.
Statement B: Under Article 200, the Governor can assent to Bills or withhold assent to Bills.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 176 concerns the Governor’s address to the State Legislature, while Article 200 permits the Governor to assent to Bills or withhold assent.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Governor nominates members to the Legislative Council when the State has one.
Statement B: The Governor nominates one-sixth of the total strength of the Legislative Council.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Governor nominates members to the Legislative Council where the State has one, and the nominated members constitute one-sixth of its total strength.

mcqs.question: The Governor appoints District Judges in consultation with which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: The Governor appoints District Judges in consultation with the High Court.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?

1. Article 361 grants immunity to the Governor.
2. No criminal proceedings can be instituted against the Governor during the Governor’s term of office.
3. Civil proceedings against the Governor can be instituted only after two months’ notice.
4. The President’s term is five years.
5. The President is removed by impeachment.
mcqs.explanation: All five statements are correct. Article 361 provides the Governor’s immunity, including protection from criminal proceedings during the term and a two-month notice requirement for civil proceedings; the President’s term is five years and removal is by impeachment.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) President's ordinance-making power
(b) President's pardoning power
(c) Governor's ordinance-making power
(d) Governor's pardoning power

List-II
(i) Article 72; all cases
(ii) Article 123
(iii) Article 161; offences against State laws
(iv) Article 213
mcqs.explanation: The President makes Ordinances under Article 123 and has pardoning power under Article 72 in all cases. The corresponding provisions for the Governor are Article 213 for Ordinances and Article 161 for offences against State laws.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The President has very limited discretionary powers.
Reason (R): The Governor has comparatively more discretionary powers than the President.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The comparatively greater discretionary powers of the Governor establish the President's discretionary powers as very limited in comparison.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Governor of Jammu and Kashmir was earlier called Sadr-e-Riyasat.
Statement B: The designation Sadr-e-Riyasat was changed to Governor in 1965.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. The earlier designation in Jammu and Kashmir was Sadr-e-Riyasat, and it was changed to Governor in 1965.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?

1. The Contingency Fund of the State is operated by the Governor.
2. The Governor decides the disqualification of MLAs under the Anti-Defection law on the advice of the Election Commission.
3. The Governor is elected.
4. The Governor is nominated or appointed.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Governor operates the State Contingency Fund, decides MLA disqualification under the Anti-Defection law on the Election Commission's advice, and is nominated or appointed rather than elected.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Governor can reserve a Bill for the President even when the Council of Ministers advises otherwise.
Reason (R): The Governor is not bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers in all matters.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Reserving a Bill for the President despite contrary advice is an exercise of the Governor's discretionary power, reflecting that the Governor is not bound by ministerial advice in all matters.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a discretionary power of the Governor?
options: Promulgating an Ordinance when the Legislature is not in session
mcqs.explanation: The dissolution of the Legislative Assembly is specifically listed as a discretionary power of the Governor.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Special responsibility in certain States
(b) Fifth Schedule
(c) Report on Scheduled Areas
(d) Sixth Schedule

List-II
(i) Includes Sixth Schedule areas and tribal areas
(ii) Special responsibility for Scheduled Areas
(iii) Report submitted to the President
(iv) Special powers regarding Autonomous District Councils
mcqs.explanation: The Governor has special responsibility in certain States, including Sixth Schedule and tribal areas; under the Fifth Schedule, the Governor is responsible for Scheduled Areas and submits a report to the President; under the Sixth Schedule, the Governor has special powers regarding Autonomous District Councils.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Governor submits a report on Scheduled Areas to the President under the Fifth Schedule.
Reason (R): Under the Fifth Schedule, the Governor has special responsibility for Scheduled Areas.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The Governor’s special responsibility for Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule is the basis for submitting a report on them to the President.

12.title: Lok Sabha Membership: Composition and Qualifications

mcqs.question: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha under Article 81?
mcqs.explanation: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552. This includes not more than 530 members from the States and not more than 20 members from the Union Territories.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding qualification for membership of the Lok Sabha is incorrect?
options: The person must be registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency.
The person must be a citizen of India.
The person must be registered as a voter in any State Legislative Assembly constituency.
The person must be at least 25 years of age.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the reference to a State Legislative Assembly constituency. The notes specify that the person must be registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years from the date of its first sitting.
Reason (R): The Lok Sabha can be dissolved earlier by the President.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. However, the President's power to dissolve the Lok Sabha earlier does not explain its normal five-year term.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Anglo-Indian nomination to the Lok Sabha was abolished after 25 January 2020 by the 104th Constitutional Amendment.
Statement B: Reservation of Lok Sabha seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was last extended by the 104th Amendment till 2030.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The notes state that Anglo-Indian nomination was abolished after 25 January 2020 and that SC/ST reservation was extended till 2030 by the 104th Amendment.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Article 81
(b) Article 83
(c) Article 84
(d) Article 330

List-II
(i) Qualification for membership
(ii) Reservation for SC/ST
(iii) Composition
(iv) Duration
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: Article 81—Composition, Article 83—Duration, Article 84—Qualification, and Article 330—Reservation for SC/ST.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Speaker.
II. A person who becomes a member of both Houses must choose one within 10 days.
III. A Minister who is not a member of either House must get elected within six months.
IV. The strength of the Council of Ministers is limited to 15% of the total membership of the Lok Sabha.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are supported by the notes. They cover the Speaker's role under the Anti-Defection Law, the ten-day choice rule, the six-month election requirement for a non-member Minister, and the 15% limit.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following are listed as conditions under which a Lok Sabha seat becomes vacant?
I. Resignation addressed to the Speaker
II. Disqualification
III. Absence for 60 days without permission
IV. Becoming a member of the other House
mcqs.explanation: All four are listed conditions for vacancy of a Lok Sabha seat. The notes specifically mention resignation to the Speaker, disqualification, unauthorised absence for 60 days, and becoming a member of the other House.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding qualification for membership of the Lok Sabha:
I. A candidate must not hold an office of profit.
II. A candidate must not be of unsound mind.
III. A candidate must not be an undischarged insolvent.
IV. Other qualifications are prescribed by the Representation of the People Act.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The listed conditions include not holding an office of profit, not being of unsound mind or an undischarged insolvent, while other qualifications are prescribed by the Representation of the People Act.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding disqualifications for Lok Sabha membership is incorrect?
options: Article 102 deals with disqualifications for Lok Sabha membership.
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 also provides for Lok Sabha disqualifications.
Article 102 deals with qualifications for Lok Sabha membership.
Disqualifications are provided under Article 102 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that Article 102 deals with qualifications. Article 102 deals with disqualifications, and Lok Sabha disqualifications are also provided under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): During a National Emergency, Parliament can extend the term of the Lok Sabha by one year at a time.
Reason (R): During a National Emergency, the President extends the Lok Sabha term by two years at a time.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The Assertion is correct: Parliament may extend the Lok Sabha term by one year at a time during a National Emergency. The Reason is false because the notes do not state that the President extends it by two years at a time.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha:
I. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes in proportion to their population.
II. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population.
III. Reservation of Lok Sabha seats was initially provided for ten years.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Lok Sabha seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population, and the reservation was initially provided for ten years.

mcqs.question: What is the quorum of the Lok Sabha?
mcqs.explanation: The quorum of the Lok Sabha is one-tenth of its total membership.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Present elected strength of the Lok Sabha
(b) Elected members from Union Territories
(c) Elected strength of the First Lok Sabha
(d) Seats held by Uttar Pradesh in the Lok Sabha

List-II
(i) 13
(ii) 80
(iii) 543
(iv) 489
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: present elected strength—543; Union Territory elected members—13; First Lok Sabha elected strength—489; Uttar Pradesh seats—80.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 102 deals with disqualifications for Lok Sabha membership.
II. Article 331 deals with Anglo-Indian representation, which is now discontinued.
III. Article 326 deals with adult suffrage.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. Articles 102, 331 and 326 respectively relate to Lok Sabha disqualifications, Anglo-Indian representation now discontinued, and adult suffrage.

mcqs.question: A person can contest elections from a maximum of how many constituencies?
mcqs.explanation: A person can contest elections from a maximum of two constituencies.

13.title: Rajya Sabha Composition and Special Powers

mcqs.question: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha according to Article 80?
mcqs.explanation: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250, comprising not more than 238 elected representatives and 12 nominated members.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding qualification for membership of the Rajya Sabha is incorrect?
options: The person must be not less than 25 years of age.
The person must be a citizen of India.
The person must be registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency.
The person must be not less than 30 years of age.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect detail is the minimum age of 25 years. For Rajya Sabha membership, the minimum age is 30 years.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha can authorise Parliament to legislate on a subject in the State List in the national interest.
Reason (R): Such authorisation requires a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha may authorise Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Article 80
(b) Article 83(1)
(c) Article 84
(d) Fourth Schedule

List-II
(i) Qualification
(ii) Allocation of seats
(iii) Composition
(iv) Duration as a permanent House
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-iii, b-iv, c-i and d-ii: Articles 80, 83(1) and 84 deal with composition, duration and qualification respectively, while the Fourth Schedule deals with allocation of seats.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Rajya Sabha is elected indirectly by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
II. The election uses proportional representation by means of the Single Transferable Vote.
III. The Rajya Sabha is subject to dissolution after every six-year term.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution, so statement III is incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: Only three Union Territories—Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir—have representation in the Rajya Sabha.
Statement B: The quorum of the Rajya Sabha is one-tenth of its total membership.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes. The three represented Union Territories are Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir, and the quorum is one-tenth of total membership.

mcqs.question: To whom is the resignation of a Rajya Sabha member addressed?
options: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
mcqs.explanation: A Rajya Sabha member addresses resignation to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, who is the Vice-President.

mcqs.question: What is the present strength of the Rajya Sabha, including elected and nominated members?
options: 245 members, comprising 233 elected and 12 nominated members
250 members, comprising 238 elected and 12 nominated members
250 members, comprising 233 elected and 17 nominated members
245 members, comprising 238 elected and 7 nominated members
mcqs.explanation: The present strength of the Rajya Sabha is 245 members, consisting of 233 elected and 12 nominated members.

mcqs.question: The allocation of seats among States in the Rajya Sabha is based on:
options: The number of Lok Sabha constituencies in each State
The number of districts in each State
mcqs.explanation: Rajya Sabha seats are allocated among States on the basis of population.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Literature
(b) Science
(c) Art
(d) Social Service

List-II
(i) Special knowledge or practical experience in literature
(ii) Special knowledge or practical experience in science
(iii) Special knowledge or practical experience in art
(iv) Special knowledge or practical experience in social service
mcqs.explanation: The President nominates persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service to the Rajya Sabha. The correct pairs are a-i, b-ii, c-iii and d-iv.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: A person seeking membership of the Rajya Sabha must not hold any office of profit.
Statement B: The other disqualifications for Rajya Sabha membership are the same as those for Lok Sabha membership under Article 102, the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and the Tenth Schedule.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are correct. Not holding an office of profit is a qualification requirement, and the other disqualifications are the same as those applicable to Lok Sabha membership under the specified provisions.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure of Rajya Sabha members:
I. The term of a Rajya Sabha member is six years.
II. Approximately one-third of the members retire every two years.
III. A casual vacancy is filled for the remainder of the term.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: a Rajya Sabha member serves for six years, about one-third retire every two years, and a casual vacancy is filled for the remaining period of the term.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha can initiate the creation of new All-India Services under Article 312.
Reason (R): The initiative under Article 312 requires a two-thirds majority of the Rajya Sabha members.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true. The two-thirds majority is the prescribed requirement for the initiative, but it does not by itself explain the Rajya Sabha’s constitutional power to initiate the creation of All-India Services under Article 312.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the powers of the Rajya Sabha:
I. It has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in Constitutional Amendment Bills.
II. It can introduce Ordinary Bills.
III. It can introduce Constitutional Amendment Bills.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Rajya Sabha has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in Constitutional Amendment Bills and can introduce both Ordinary Bills and Constitutional Amendment Bills.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements regarding Lok Sabha membership are correct?
I. The minimum age for Lok Sabha membership is 25 years.
II. The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 members.
III. The Lok Sabha is elected directly.
IV. The term of a Lok Sabha member is five years.
mcqs.explanation: All four statements are correct. The minimum age is 25 years, the maximum strength is 552, election is direct, and the term is five years.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements regarding the Lok Sabha are correct?
I. The Lok Sabha can be dissolved.
II. The Lok Sabha has no nominated members.
III. Anglo-Indian nomination to the Lok Sabha has been abolished.
mcqs.explanation: All three listed statements are correct: the Lok Sabha can be dissolved, it has no nominated members, and Anglo-Indian nomination has been abolished.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Rajya Sabha’s role in relation to a Money Bill is incorrect?
options: It must deal with a Money Bill within 14 days.
Its role is limited to recommending changes to the Money Bill.
It can only recommend changes to a Money Bill.
It introduces the Money Bill and has the final say on it.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that the Rajya Sabha introduces the Money Bill and has the final say. According to the notes, it can only recommend changes and must do so within 14 days; the Lok Sabha introduces the Money Bill and has the final say.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Lok Sabha introduces Money Bills and has the final say on them.
Reason (R): The Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes to a Money Bill within 14 days.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: The Lok Sabha introduces Money Bills and has the final say. The Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes within 14 days, which explains the Lok Sabha’s final authority.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) First nominated woman member of the Rajya Sabha
(b) Year associated with the first nominated woman member
(c) State with the highest number of Rajya Sabha seats
(d) Authority deciding questions concerning anti-defection in the Rajya Sabha

List-II
(i) Chairman
(ii) Uttar Pradesh
(iii) 1980
(iv) Nargis Du
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are: first nominated woman member—Nargis Du; year—1980; state with the highest number of seats—Uttar Pradesh; anti-defection decision—Chairman.

mcqs.question: The Objectives Resolution, on which the Preamble was based, was adopted on:
mcqs.explanation: The Objectives Resolution was moved by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Sovereign
(b) Socialist
(c) Republic
(d) Fraternity

List-II
(i) Head of the State is elected
(ii) Assuring dignity of the individual and unity and integrity of the Nation
(iii) Supreme authority; free from external control
(iv) Aims at reducing inequality
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Sovereign–supreme authority, Socialist–reducing inequality, Republic–elected head of State, and Fraternity–dignity, unity and integrity.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The LIC of India Case in 1995 reaffirmed that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The LIC of India Case, 1995, reaffirmed the Preamble’s status as an integral part of the Constitution.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added the words ‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and ‘Integrity’.
The Berubari Union Case of 1960 held that the Preamble was not a part of the Constitution.
The Preamble is justiciable and can be enforced in a court of law.
The Preamble has been amended only once so far.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is the fourth one. The notes state that the Preamble is non-justiciable and cannot be enforced in a court of law.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

I. The date mentioned in the Preamble is 26 November 1949.
II. The word ‘Federal’ is not mentioned in the Preamble.
III. The Preamble itself confers powers and creates rights.
IV. The Preamble can be amended under Article 368.
mcqs.explanation: Statements I, II and IV are correct. The Preamble does not itself confer any power or create any right, so Statement III is incorrect.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The idea of the Preamble was borrowed from the Constitution of the USA.
Statement B: The language of the Preamble was influenced by the Australian Constitution.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true according to the notes: the idea was borrowed from the USA, while the language was influenced by the Australian Constitution.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following cases in chronological order:

A. Kesavananda Bharati Case
B. LIC of India Case
C. Berubari Union Case
D. Golaknath Case
mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence is Berubari Union Case (1960), Golaknath Case (1967), Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973), and LIC of India Case (1995).

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Preamble can be amended, but its Basic Structure cannot be altered.
Reason (R): The Kesavananda Bharati Case of 1973 held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, but the Basic Structure cannot be destroyed.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
